comparacio: Up slightly from 3.217% on Tuesday. November's provisional average is 3.262%; October closed at 3.239%, and a year ago (November 2025) it was 2.217%.
que_vol_dir: It's the index behind most variable-rate mortgages in Spain. If yours is reset this month using October's average, on a €167,000 mortgage over 25 years at Euribor + 0.75%, the monthly payment goes from about €789 to about €880: around €91 more.
hi_guanya: Savers: deposits and interest-paying accounts tend to pay more.
hi_perd: People with a variable-rate mortgage that's due for review.
per_a_leconomia: It makes credit more expensive for households and businesses: fewer mortgages and fewer investment loans are taken out, which cools home buying and construction.

comparacio: Flash estimate for October, the same as in September. Core inflation, excluding energy and fresh food, is 3.1%.
que_vol_dir: What cost €100 a year ago now costs €104.90 on average. Money sitting idle loses that much purchasing power every year.
hi_guanya: People with fixed-rate debts: in real terms, what they owe is worth less.
hi_perd: People with savings that earn nothing and people whose pay isn't adjusted for inflation.
per_a_leconomia: With high inflation, wages and business costs tend to rise and the ECB comes under pressure to raise rates, which slows activity. Companies that can't pass costs on to their prices see their margins squeezed.

comparacio: 45% lower than yesterday (€210.94/MWh), the day after the general strike. Cheapest hour, 1–2 pm (€1.09/MWh); most expensive, 8–9 pm (€196.29/MWh).
que_vol_dir: This is the energy price before network charges and taxes. On Spain's regulated tariff (PVPC), a kWh costs €0.041 today from 2 to 3 pm and €0.350 from 8 to 9 pm: a 2 kWh wash costs about 8 cents at midday and about 70 cents in the evening.
hi_guanya: People who can run the washing machine or oven at midday, when there's more solar power.
hi_perd: People on the regulated tariff who use most of their power between 8 and 9 pm.
per_a_leconomia: Expensive electricity is a direct cost for industry (metals, chemicals, food): it makes factories less competitive and ends up pushing up the price of many products.

comparacio: Petrol is down 3 cents in a week (€1.732/l on 29 October) and diesel 1 cent (€1.899/l). The cut in fuel duty remains in place in November.
que_vol_dir: Filling a 50-litre tank with petrol costs about €85, €1.50 less than the week before; with diesel, about €94.
hi_perd: The public purse, which collects less in tax.
per_a_leconomia: Freight transport runs on diesel: when it gets cheaper, so does moving everything that travels by lorry. The tax cut, however, means less public revenue.

comparacio: Unchanged since the 29 October meeting. Chief economist Philip Lane says a December hike would be "very prudent" if the data don't change, and markets already price it in.
que_vol_dir: It's the official price of money in the euro area. When the ECB raises it, loans and mortgages get more expensive and savings pay more; it's how the ECB reins in inflation.
hi_guanya: Savers, if the ECB does end up raising rates.
hi_perd: Anyone who needs financing: households with loans and businesses.
per_a_leconomia: Interest rates are the economy's brake and accelerator: keeping them high curbs inflation, but also business investment and job creation.

comparacio: Rate at the November auction, slightly above October's 3.026% and the highest since July 2024. Bids totalled €6,846m and €4,045m was sold.
que_vol_dir: Lending €1,000 to the Spanish state for a year earns you about €31 before tax. With inflation at 4.9%, though, you still lose purchasing power: it's a way to lose less, not to gain.
hi_guanya: Cautious savers who want a safe short-term return.
hi_perd: The state, which pays more to borrow.
per_a_leconomia: If the state pays more to borrow, it has less left for other spending. And because government debt is the benchmark for many loans, borrowing also gets more expensive for businesses.
